title: Talent Nation raises pre-seed round to train one million African AI engineers

claims.text: Talent Nation, a startup founded by Nigerian serial entrepreneur Iyinoluwa Aboyeji and South African-born entrepreneur Kesiah Valkin, has raised an undisclosed pre-seed round.
It aims to train and deploy one million AI engineers from Africa into businesses worldwide over the next decade.
The round was co-led by Enza Capital and London-based LocalGlobe, with participation from Future Africa, Kaleo Ventures, Ajim Capital, Solving.org and Accelerate Africa.
Through its Learn2Earn academy, Talent Nation trains, certifies and deploys engineers into organisations that want to build and manage their own AI capabilities.
Aboyeji, the executive chairman, co-founded Andela and Flutterwave, according to Semafor.
The company has not disclosed the size of the round or a detailed timetable for reaching its target.
Aboyeji says Talent Nation wants to make certified AI engineering talent accessible to organisations at a fraction of the cost of hiring from frontier AI labs or traditional consulting firms.
Aboyeji told Semafor that Learn2Earn received 63,000 applications, and fewer than 3% were selected for training on multiple campuses.
claims.label: Learn2Earn applications

claims.text: Aboyeji told Semafor that most developers from the training programmes will be African, though he does not want to constrain the company to that.
The venture mirrors Andela, which Aboyeji launched in 2014 and which trained a generation of software engineers in six African countries, according to Semafor.
Companies are adopting AI quickly, but many struggle to find engineers who can build and maintain reliable systems around AI models, according to TechAwk NG.
